obernants.approximation_semantics: Mathematical target with bounded finite evidence, not a proof.
obernants.assumptions: Ordinary Rust execution, sufficient allocation, byte equality.
obernants.domain: All finite byte slices and returned usize vector observations.
obernants.operator: Universe: finite byte inputs paired with arbitrary usize vectors. Excluded outputs have incorrect length, z[0] != n when n>0, a radius beyond the suffix, an unequal byte inside a claimed match, or an extendable nonmaximal radius. This mathematical exclusion relation is not replaced by negative tests.

obernants.approximation_semantics: Mathematical target with bounded finite evidence, not a proof.
obernants.assumptions: Ordinary Rust execution, sufficient allocation, byte equality.
obernants.domain: All finite byte slices and returned usize vector observations.
obernants.operator: Given vector v, compatible antecedents are all byte strings s with length n=v.len(), 0<=v[i]<=n-i for every index i, v[0]=n when nonempty, equalities s[j]=s[i+j] for j<v[i], and inequality s[v[i]]!=s[i+v[i]] whenever i+v[i]<n. Empty vector admits only empty input. Constraints can be inconsistent; symbol names are not recoverable uniquely.

obernants.domain: All finite byte slices and returned usize vector observations.
obernants.operator: Every injective relabeling of byte symbols preserves the prefix vector. A constant string of length n yields [n,n-1,...,1].

obernants.approximation_semantics: Exact mathematical target under assumptions; bounded executed evidence only.
obernants.assumptions: Ordinary successful Rust execution, sufficient allocation and exact byte equality. Mathematical sums; test sums fit usize. Finite fixtures do not establish unrestricted correctness.
obernants.domain: Candidate vectors v of length n<=256, byte witnesses.
obernants.falsifiable_check: equality_constraints_reconstruct_and_reject rejects [3,2,0] despite legal bounds and roundtrips five witnesses.
obernants.observation_scope: Named relations and bounded source correspondence fixtures.
obernants.operator: Require v[0]=n for n>0 and v[i]<=n-i. Quotient positions by j~i+j for j<v[i]. Add inequality edges (v[i],i+v[i]) when i+v[i]<n. Feasible iff no edge is a quotient self-loop: assign distinct bytes to classes. For n>256 general feasibility additionally requires quotient graph 256-colorability.

obernants.domain: Nonempty input s of length n, integers 1<=p<=n.
obernants.falsifiable_check: borders_periods_and_prefix_occurrences compares each p to literal slices; ababa refutes divisibility.
obernants.observation_scope: Named relations and bounded source correspondence fixtures.
obernants.operator: p is a period iff s[p..n]=s[0..n-p], iff p=n or z[p]=n-p. For p<n this is exactly a border of length n-p. Periods need not divide n; divisibility additionally characterizes whole-block repetition.

obernants.operator: Occurrence starts of s[0..k] are exactly {i:z[i]>=k}. Count=sum_i 1[z[i]>=k]. Retaining positions recovers the occurrence observation, not original symbols.

obernants.operator: h merges full-vector fibers: abca yields [4,0,0,1] and aabc yields [4,1,0,0], both sum five. h cannot recover positions or z. Neither input reversal nor noninjective symbol maps generally preserve z.
